names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 mai, «Sfântul Ierarh Gherman, Patriarhul Constantinopolului».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Γερμανός Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 12 May, „Свети Герман, патријарх цариградски.“ — Свети left off, which is not a rank, and „патријарх цариградски“ left off, which is the `patriarch` this folder already carries in `types` and the see this corpus puts in `office`. The heading gives no epithet; the senator father, the castration, Cyzicus, Copronymus, Leo the Isaurian and the 740 are all in the body. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Герман, so the form folds with nothing — the corpus's four other Germani, of Dobrogea, of Novgorod, of Sagmata and of Kazan, having no Serbian form.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 511 as the day page prints it, «Святитель Герман Константинопольский, патриарх», with the rank words left off; his life page is headed «Святитель Герман, Патриарх Константинопольский». The day's own line declines him «Свт. Германа , патриарха Константинопольского (740).» `fk.mjs` on «Герман Константинопольский» returned NONE before the write.

death.note: The first date this folder has carried. The Ohrid Prologue, for the Julian 12 May: „отера у манастир, где овај светитељ проживе још десет година, док га Господ не позва к Себи у Царство небеско 740. године.“ — and the folder's own Greek attestation note records saint.gr giving the same year, a death at Platania at the age of a hundred on 12 May 740, so the two books agree and nothing is widened. **No birth is recorded**: the Prologue gives none, and saint.gr's 640 was not lifted because that page was not opened by this reader. The ten years in the monastery after his deposition are the book's own and are consistent with the 740; they were not turned into a second number.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 мая ст. ст. — «Свт. Германа , патриарха Константинопольского (740).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the other three churches, and the same man: the patriarch of Constantinople who withstood the iconoclasts under Лев III Исавр, laid down his omophorion and died in 740. The Russian life page, life1047, heads «День памяти: 12 мая» and lists no other day. **The day page's two hymns are headed «святителей Епифания и Германа», for him and for the bishop of Cyprus together, and both are copied here and on that folder** — the troparion is the common of holy fathers, «Боже отец наших», and the kontakion names the two of them. The line gives 740, which is the year the folder already carries, so `dates` were not touched. The Russian life adds his age at death, ninety-five, and the length of his patriarchate, fourteen years and five months; neither was made a bound, because a lifespan subtracted from a death is a calculation and not a year any book prints, and the folder's own date note already refuses the same operation on the Prologue's figure. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 mai — «Sfântul Ierarh Gherman, Patriarhul Constantinopolului»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Γερμανός Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: the patriarch who would not obey Leo the Isaurian's iconoclast decrees, laid his omophorion on the holy table and resigned. **He is none of the corpus's four other Germani** — of Dobrogea, of Novgorod, of Sagmata — whom the namesweep flagged and which were read. **The Greek adds the years the corpus does not hold**: born at Constantinople in 640, son of the patrician Justinian whom Constantine Pogonatos put to death, made metropolitan of Cyzicus at thirty-seven, patriarch in 715, dead at Platania at the age of a hundred on 12 May 740 and buried in the monastery of Chora. **The existing `dates` object is not touched** and those years stand here and in the added paragraph instead. **The apolytikion taken is the joint hymn of the pair**, Ἦχος α’ Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντα, which names Germanus first and Epiphanius second and is the service of the two hierarchs the day keeps together; it is their common and not a mis-hang, and it is copied whole with that said. The page also prints a second apolytikion of the pair and a kontakion of the pair. **`hymnographer` is added to `types`** on the page's own count of what survived Leo's burning of his books: 104 stichera and 22 canons.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.05.2026 (12. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Герман, патријарх цариградски.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep him on, so nothing moved. **A FIRST DATE FOR A FOLDER THAT HELD NONE, AND TWO BOOKS AGREE ON IT**: „док га Господ не позва к Себи у Царство небеско 740. године“ — and this folder's own Greek note records saint.gr putting his death at Platania in 740, so `dates` gains a `death` of 740 where there was no `dates` object at all and nothing is widened. **saint.gr's 640, its thirty-seven years and its 715 were NOT lifted**: that page was not opened by this reader, and a year read out of another reader's note is not a year read. The book's own „проживе још десет година“ in the monastery after his deposition is consistent with the 740 and was not turned into a second number. **New here, and none of it in the Romanian or the Greek account this folder was built from**: **that Constantine Pogonatus, having killed his father the first imperial senator, had this son of his castrated and drove him by force into a monastery** — the Greek had the father's death and not the mutilation; that as a monk he shone like a star by his virtuous life, and was for that elected first bishop of Cyzicus and then, when Anastasius II came to the throne, patriarch of Constantinople; **that as patriarch he baptised the ill-famed Copronymus, who fouled the water at the font, and prophesied then that the child, when he became emperor, would bring some unclean heresy into the Holy Church — which came to pass, Copronymus renewing the iconoclast heresy when he reigned**; that Leo the Isaurian, Copronymus's father, began the persecution of the icons, and that when the patriarch opposed him **the overbearing Leo cried „Ја сам цар и свештеник!“ — I am emperor and priest** — and threw Germanus off his throne and drove him to a monastery, where he lived ten years more. **`monk` WAS READ AND REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL WAS MEASURED.** „Као монах, Герман засветли као звезда“ is the book's own word for what he was, and §5's table reads Монах as `monk`; but `lib/honorific.js` counts `monk` among the monastics that compose `venerable`, which stands **above** `confessor` in its precedence — so adding it would make this folder read „Venerable Germanus of Constantinople“ where it reads „Confessor Germanus of Constantinople“. Measured with `node -e` against that file before anything was written. **That is a conflicting rank and not the missing rank `types_add` is for**, and the forced tonsure is in the life instead. `patriarch`, `hierarch`, `confessor` and `hymnographer` all stand untouched. **No saint but Epiphanius is named in the appended paragraphs**, and he was already a `related` row in both directions; Constantine Pogonatus, Anastasius II, Copronymus and Leo the Isaurian have no folders in this corpus, which was checked. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Dumnezeul părinţilor noştri, Care faci pururea cu noi după blândeţile Tale, nu depărta mila Ta de la noi; ci pentru rugăciunile lor, în pace îndreptează viaţa noastră.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Gherman, Patriarhul Constantinopolului», Glasul 4; the page prints the common troparion of the holy fathers, in the plural — «pentru rugăciunile lor» — and the same text stands on this calendar's page for Epiphanius of Cyprus on the same day

english.text: O God of our fathers, who ever dealest with us according to Thy gentleness: take not Thy mercy from us, but by their prayers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Ξυνωρίδα τῆς θείας Ἐκκλησίας τᾶς σάλπιγγας, Γερμανὸν σοφὸν Ἱεράρχην, καὶ κλεινὸν Ἐπιφάνιον, τιμήσωμεν προφρόνως οἱ πιστοί, τὸν μὲν ὡς ἐν φρονήματι στερρῶ ὑπὲρ τῆς Χριστοῦ εἰκόνος, τὸν θεομάχον Λέοντα ἐλέγξαντα, ὡς μάστιγα δὲ αἱρέσεων δεινήν, τὸν ἅγιον Ἐπιφάνιον, Οὗτοι γὰρ ἐκτενῶς ὑπὲρ ἠμῶν, ἀεὶ πρεσβεύουσι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντα, on the page of Άγιος Γερμανός Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης — the joint hymn of the two hierarchs the day keeps

english.text: Let us the faithful honour with a ready mind the pair of trumpets of the divine Church, Germanus the wise hierarch and renowned Epiphanius: the one for rebuking, in a mind unshaken for the icon of Christ, Leo the fighter against God; the other, holy Epiphanius, as a dread scourge of heresies. For these two intercede earnestly and always for us.

hymns.text: Боже отец наших,/ творяй присно с нами по Твоей кротости,/ не отстави милость Твою от нас,/ но молитвами их/ в мире управи живот наш.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 мая ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителей Епифания и Германа»

english.text: O God of our fathers, who ever dealest with us according to Thy gentleness, take not Thy mercy from us, but by their prayers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Священноначальник чудную двоицу восхвалим, вернии, по долгу,/ с Германом Божественнаго Епифания:/ сии бо попалиша безбожных языки,/ догматы премудрейшия возложше всем,/ православно поющим присно благочестия великое таинство.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 мая ст. ст. — «Кондак святителей Епифания и Германа»

english.text: Let us the faithful praise as we ought the wondrous pair of hierarchs, the divine Epiphanius together with Germanus; for they burned up the tongues of the godless, setting forth most wise doctrines for all who sing ever in the Orthodox manner the great mystery of godliness.
